title: UX Design students share health and robotics concepts for faculty review
summary: Chorong Park's students presented health-focused design concepts and received feedback on users, physical interaction and the evidence behind their ideas.

sources.label: Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post and classroom photographs
Stanford Center on Longevity's 2026-2027 Design Challenge

paragraphs.text: Students in Chorong Park's Introduction to UX Design course at the University of Houston presented health-focused app and robotics concepts for faculty review on November 12. Their projects explored nutrition and daily planning, dementia care, home rehabilitation, stress and sleep, sobriety support, and wearable EEG monitoring.

Park described a semester of reading scientific literature, interviewing people, running surveys and testing prototypes. These activities helped students revisit their assumptions. One team explored how a robot might help students make food choices and plan their day around nutritional needs.

Faculty feedback asked teams to identify their users more precisely, explain what physical interaction adds, and examine their technical and business assumptions. For Park, the lesson goes beyond making an appealing concept: design decisions need a clear purpose and evidence behind them.

The teams plan to use that feedback to refine their work for submission to the Stanford Center on Longevity Design Challenge. Its 2026-2027 theme is Human-Centered Robotics for Longevity. Park hopes students gain both confidence in developing ideas and the judgment to question them.

review.notes: Complete caption and author checked using Read more in the connected feed and on the original LinkedIn page. All nine observed gallery images were downloaded, visually inspected and preserved byte-for-byte in source order, with dimensions and SHA-256 recorded.
